kind.description:
The webhook kind indicates how and when it is called.

ENRICHING webhooks are called before rendering the certificate template. They have two functions. First, they must allow the certificate request or it will be aborted. Second, they can return additional data to be referenced in the certificate template. The payload sent to the webhook server varies based on whether an X509 or SSH certificate is to be signed and based on the type of provisioner.
 Allowed values: `ENRICHING`

name.description: The name of the webhook. For `ENRICHING` webhooks, the returned data can be referenced in the certificate under the path `.Webhooks.<name>`. Must be unique to the provisioner.

secret.description: The shared secret used to authenticate the payload sent to the webhook server. Generated server-side. This is returned only for `EXTERNAL` webhook servers and only once, at the time of creation.

server_type.description:
An EXTERNAL webhook server is not operated by Smallstep. The caller must use the returned ID and secret to configure the server.

A HOSTED_ATTESTATION webhook server is hosted by Smallstep and must be used with an `ENRICHING` webhook type and an ACME Attestation provisioner. The webhook server will verify the attested permanent identifier exists as the ID of an instance in the configured collection. The data of the instance in the collection will be added to the template data.
 Allowed values: `EXTERNAL` `HOSTED_ATTESTATION`

source.description: Registration sources that devices must match. Allowed values: `End-User` `Smallstep API` `Smallstep Agent` `Jamf` `Intune`

policy.description: Policy to select the devices an account is assigned to. An empty policy indicates an account will be provisioned for all devices.

approved_at.description: Timestamp in RFC3339 format when the device was approved to connect to company resources. Read only.

connected.description: The device is currently connected to Smallstep. Read only.

display_id.description:
An opaque identifier that may be used to link this device to an external inventory.
This field may be populated with a value derived from data synced from your team's MDMs.
Setting this value explicitly will mask any MDM-derived value.

display_name.description:
A friendly name for the device.
This field may be populated with a value derived from data synced from your team's MDMs.
Setting this value explicitly will mask any MDM-derived value.

enrolled_at.description: Timestamp in RFC3339 format when the device first connected to Smallstep. Read only.

high_assurance.description: The device has been issued certificates using high assurance device attestation. Read only.

host_id.description: The identifier for the smallstep agent on the device.

id.description: A UUID identifying this device. Read only.

last_seen.description: Timestamp in RFC3339 format when the device last connected to Smallstep. Read only.

metadata.description: A map of key-value pairs available as template data when a provisioner with a webhook is used to issue a certificate to a device.

os.description:
The device operating system.
This field may be populated with a value derived from data synced from your team's MDMs.
Setting this value explicitly will mask any MDM-derived value.
 Allowed values: `Linux` `Windows` `macOS` `iOS` `tvOS` `watchOS` `visionOS`

ownership.description:
Whether the device is owned by the user or the company.
This field may be populated with a value derived from data synced from your team's MDMs.
Setting this value explicitly will mask any MDM-derived value.
 Allowed values: `company` `user`

permanent_identifier.description: The cryptographic identity of the device. High-assurance devices are only issued certificates when this identifier is attested by a trusted source. All devices with the same permanent identifier appear as a single device in the Smallstep API. For Windows and Linux devices this is the hash of the TPM endorsement key and for Apple devices it is the serial number.

serial.description:
The serial number of the device.
This field may be populated with a value derived from data synced from your team's MDMs.
Setting this value explicitly will mask any MDM-derived value.

tags.description: A set of tags that can be used to group devices.

display_name.description: Full name of the user the device is assigned to. Synced from team's identity provider. Read only.

email.description:
Email of the user the device is assigned to.
This field may be populated with a value derived from data synced from your team's MDMs.
Setting this value explicitly will mask any MDM-derived value.

user.description: The user that a device is assigned to. A device cannot be approved for high-assurance certificates until a user has been assigned to it.

block.description: A device represents a computer that can be issued x509 certificates for securely connecting to company resources.

autojoin.description: Whether or not clients should automatically connect to the network.

credentials.description: The UUID of credentials that the Smallstep agent will configure to use this ethernet integration.

id.description: The UUID of this protected Ethernet configuration.

name.description: A human-friendly display name for this resource.

radius_server_ca.description: The certificate bundle used to verify the RADIUS server.

block.description: Configuration for connecting a device to an EAP-TLS 802.1X wired network.

issuer.description: The URL of this identity provider.

jwks_endpoint.description: The URL where relying parties can read the provider's public key.

token_endpoint.description: The URL where relying parties exchange authorization codes for identity tokens.

trust_roots.description: The CA used to verify clients at the authorize endpoint.

id.description: The client ID.

redirect_uri.description: Where user-agents will be sent after authentication attempts.

client_ca.description: The CA that the RADIUS server will trust to verify clients.

id.description: The UUID of this managed RADIUS server.

name.description: A descriptive name for this resource. Must be unique across the team.

nas_ips.description: The IP addresses the Network Access Server (NAS) may connect from to the RADIUS server.

name.description: The attribute name.

value_from_certificate.description: The object identifier (OID) of a field in the supplicant certificate. The RADIUS server will set the value of the reply attribute to the value of the field.

server_ca.description: The CA that supplicants should use to verify the RADIUS server.

server_hostname.description: The hostname of the RADIUS server.

server_ip.description: The IP address of the RADIUS server.

server_port.description: The port of the RADIUS server.

id.description: The UUID of a managed RADIUS resource.

secret.description: The secret a network access server needs to authenticate to a managed RADIUS server.

block.description: Read the secret required to configure a network access server to connect to a managed RADIUS server.

challenges.description: Which ACME challenge types are allowed. Allowed values: `http-01` `dns-01` `tls-alpn-01`

force_cn.description: Force one of the SANs to become the Common Name, if a Common Name is not provided.

require_eab.description: Only ACME clients that have been preconfigured with valid EAB credentials will be able to create an account with this provisioner. Must be `true` for all new provisioners.

acme.description: A [provisioner](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/provisioners/#acme) that enables automation with the [ACME protocol](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/acme-basics/#acme-challenges). This object is populated when type is `ACME`.

attestation_formats.description: The allowed attestation formats for the device-attest-01 challenge. Valid values are `apple`, `step`, and `tpm`. The apple format is for Apple devices, and adds trust for Apple's CAs. The step format is for non-TPM devices that can issue attestation certificates, such as YubiKey PIV. It adds trust for Yubico's root CA. The tpm format is for TPMs and does not trust any CAs by default. Allowed values: `apple` `step` `tpm`

attestation_roots.description: A trust bundle of root certificates in PEM format that will be used to verify attestation certificates. The default value depends on the value of attestationFormats. If provided, this PEM bundle will override the CA trust established by setting attestationFormats to apple or step. At least one root certificate is required when using the tpm attestationFormat.

force_cn.description: Force one of the SANs to become the Common Name, if a Common Name is not provided.

require_eab.description: Only ACME clients that have been preconfigured with valid EAB credentials will be able to create an account with this provisioner.

acme_attestation.description: A [provisioner](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/provisioners/#acme) that enables automation with the [device-attest-01 challenge of the ACME protocol](https://smallstep.com/blog/acme-managed-device-attestation-explained/). This object is populated when type is `ACME_ATTESTATION`.

authority_id.description: The UUID of the authority this provisioner is attached to

accounts.description: The list of AWS account IDs that are allowed to use an AWS cloud provisioner.

disable_custom_sans.description: By default custom SANs are valid, but if this option is set to `true` only the SANs available in the instance identity document will be valid. These are the private IP and the DNS ip-<private-ip>.<region>.compute.internal.

disable_trust_on_first_use.description: By default only one certificate will be granted per instance, but if the option is set to `true` this limit is not set and different tokens can be used to get different certificates.

instance_age.description: The maximum age of an instance that should be allowed to obtain a certificate. Limits certificate issuance to new instances to mitigate the risk of credential-misuse from instances that don't need a certificate. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

aws.description: The [AWS provisioner](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/provisioners/#aws) grants a certificate to an Amazon EC2 instance using the Instance Identity Document. This object is populated when type is `AWS`.

audience.description: Defaults to https://management.azure.com/ but it can be changed if necessary.

disable_custom_sans.description: By default custom SANs are valid, but if this option is set to `true` only the SANs available in the token will be valid, in Azure only the virtual machine name is available.

disable_trust_on_first_use.description: By default only one certificate will be granted per instance, but if the option is set to true this limit is not set and different tokens can be used to get different certificates.

resource_groups.description: The list of resource group names that are allowed to use this provisioner.

tenant_id.description: The Azure account tenant ID for this provisioner. This ID is the Directory ID available in the Azure Active Directory properties.

azure.description: The [Azure provisioner](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/provisioners/#azure) grants certificates to Microsoft Azure instances using the managed identities tokens. This object is populated when type is `AZURE`.

allow_renewal_after_expiry.description: Allow renewals for expired certificates generated by this provisioner.

default_host_ssh_cert_duration.description: The default duration for an SSH host certificate generated by this provisioner. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

default_tls_cert_duration.description: The default duration for an x509 certificate generated by this provisioner. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

default_user_ssh_cert_duration.description: The default duration for an SSH user certificate generated by this provisioner. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

disable_renewal.description: Disable renewal for all certificates generated by this provisioner.

enable_ssh_ca.description: Allow this provisioner to be used to generate SSH certificates.

max_host_ssh_cert_duration.description: The maximum duration for an SSH host certificate generated by this provisioner. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

max_tls_cert_duration.description: The maximum duration for an x509 certificate generated by this provisioner. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

max_user_ssh_cert_duration.description: The maximum duration for an SSH user certificate generated by this provisioner. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

min_host_ssh_cert_duration.description: The minimum duration for an SSH host certificate generated by this provisioner. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

min_tls_cert_duration.description: The minimum duration for an x509 certificate generated by this provisioner. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

min_user_ssh_cert_duration.description: The minimum duration for an SSH user certificate generated by this provisioner. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

claims.description: A set of constraints configuring how this provisioner can be used to issue certificates.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the provisioner was created in RFC 3339 format. Generated server-side.

disable_custom_sans.description: By default custom SANs are valid, but if this option is set to `true` only the SANs available in the instance identity document will be valid, these are the DNS `<instance-name>.c.<project-id>.internal` and `<instance-name>.<zone>.c.<project-id>.internal`.

disable_trust_on_first_use.description: By default only one certificate will be granted per instance, but if the option is set to `true` this limit is not set and different tokens can be used to get different certificates.

instance_age.description: The maximum age of an instance that should be allowed to obtain a certificate. Limits certificate issuance to new instances to mitigate the risk of credential-misuse from instances that don't need a certificate. Parsed as a [Golang duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration).

project_ids.description: The list of project identifiers that are allowed to use a GCP cloud provisioner.

service_accounts.description: The list of service accounts that are allowed to use a GCP cloud provisioner.

gcp.description: The [GCP provisioner](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/provisioners/#gcp) grants a certificate to a Google Compute Engine instance using its identity token. At least one service account or project ID must be set. This object is populated when type is `GCP`.

id.description: A UUID identifying this provisioner. Generated server-side when the provisioner is created. Either id or name must be set.

jwk.description: A [provisioner](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/provisioners/#jwk) that uses public-key cryptography to sign and validate a JSON Web Token (JWT). This object is populated when type is `JWK`.

name.description: The name of the provisioner. Either id or name must be set.

admins.description: The emails of admin users in an OpenID Connect provisioner. These users will not have restrictions in the certificates to sign.

client_id.description: The id used to validate the audience in an OpenID Connect token.

client_secret.description: The secret used to obtain the OpenID Connect tokens.

domains.description: The domains used to validate the email claim in an OpenID Connect provisioner.

groups.description: The group list used to validate the groups extension in an OpenID Connect token.

listen_address.description: The callback address used in the OpenID Connect flow.

tenant_id.description: The tenant-id used to replace the templatized tenantid value in the OpenID Configuration.

oidc.description: A [provisioner](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/provisioners/#oauthoidc-single-sign-on) that is configured to trust and accept an OAuth provider's ID tokens for authentication. By default, the issued certificate will use the subject (sub) claim from the identity token as its subject. The value of the token's email claim is also included as an email SAN in the certificate. This object is populated when type is `OIDC`.

template.description: A JSON representation of the SSH certificate to be created. [More info](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/templates/#ssh-templates).

template_data.description: A map of data that can be used by the certificate template.

ssh.description: Options that apply when issuing SSH certificates

template.description: A JSON representation of the x509 certificate to be created. [More info](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/templates/#x509-templates).

template_data.description: A map of data that can be used by the certificate template.

x509.description: Options that apply when issuing x509 certificates.

options.description: Options that apply when issuing certificates with this provisioner.

type.description: The type of provisioner. Allowed values: `OIDC` `JWK` `ACME` `ACME_ATTESTATION` `X5C` `AWS` `GCP` `AZURE` `SCEP`

roots.description: A list of pem-encoded x509 certificates. Any certificate bundle that chains up to any of these roots can be used in a certificate request.

x5c.description: A [provisioner](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/provisioners/#x5c---x509-certificate) that authenticates a certificate request with an existing x509 certificate. This object is populated when type is `X5C`.

block.description: [Provisioners](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/provisioners/) are methods of using the CA to get certificates with different modes of authorization.

disable_tls_client_auth.description: The CA will not send a client certificate when requested by the webhook server. Optional for `EXTERNAL` webhook servers; not allowed with hosted webhook servers.

id.description: UUID identifying this webhook. Generated server-side when the webhook is created. Will be sent to the webhook server in every request in the `X-Smallstep-Webhook-ID` header.

kind.description:
The webhook kind indicates how and when it is called.

ENRICHING webhooks are called before rendering the certificate template. They have two functions. First, they must allow the certificate request or it will be aborted. Second, they can return additional data to be referenced in the certificate template. The payload sent to the webhook server varies based on whether an X509 or SSH certificate is to be signed and based on the type of provisioner.
 Allowed values: `ENRICHING`

name.description: The name of the webhook. For `ENRICHING` webhooks, the returned data can be referenced in the certificate under the path `.Webhooks.<name>`. Must be unique to the provisioner.

server_type.description:
An EXTERNAL webhook server is not operated by Smallstep. The caller must use the returned ID and secret to configure the server.

A HOSTED_ATTESTATION webhook server is hosted by Smallstep and must be used with an `ENRICHING` webhook type and an ACME Attestation provisioner. The webhook server will verify the attested permanent identifier exists as the ID of an instance in the configured collection. The data of the instance in the collection will be added to the template data.
 Allowed values: `EXTERNAL` `HOSTED_ATTESTATION`

url.description: The URL of the webhook server. Required for `EXTERNAL` webhook servers; read-only for hosted webhook servers.

block.description: A [webhook](https://smallstep.com/docs/step-ca/webhooks/) to call when a certificate request is being processed.

autojoin.description: Whether or not clients should automatically connect to the network.

connection_type.description: The type of VPN connection. Allowed values: `IPsec` `IKEv2` `SSL`

credentials.description: The UUID of credentials that the Smallstep agent will configure to use this VPN integration.

id.description: The UUID of this protected VPN configuration.

ca_chain.description: The certificate authority bundle that client certificates must chain up to.

eap.description: Whether or not EAP is enforced on this VPN server.

remote_id.description: Typically, the common name of the remote server. Defaults to the remote address.

ike.description: Configuration for VPNs that use the IKEv2 protocol.

name.description: A human-friendly display name for this configuration.

remote_address.description: The public IP address of the VPN server.

vendor.description: For SSL-type VPN connections, the vendor of the VPN. Allowed values: `F5` `Cisco` `Juniper`

block.description: Configuration to use a credential to connect a device to a VPN.

autojoin.description: Whether or not clients should automatically connect to the network.

credentials.description: The UUID of credentials that the Smallstep agent will configure to use this Wi-Fi integration.

hidden.description: Whether or not the SSID is broadcast by the access points.

id.description: The UUID of this protected Wi-Fi configuration.

name.description: A human-friendly display name for this resource.

radius_server_ca.description: The certificate bundle used to verify the RADIUS server.

radius_server_domain.description: Require the RADIUS server certificate to contain this DNS name as a SAN or CommonName. Supported on Windows.

ssid.description: The name of the wireless network that clients connect to.

block.description: Configuration to use a credential to connect to a protected Wi-Fi network.
